title: HackTricks Cloud
summary: An encyclopedic collection of cloud pentesting techniques for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and CI/CD. Actively maintained by the HackTricks wiki.

title: flaws.cloud
summary: Scott Piper's classic six-level AWS misconfiguration CTF. Still the canonical first introduction to AWS security.

title: flaws2.cloud
summary: You play the same scenario twice: once as the attacker, once as the defender reading CloudTrail logs. Teaches exploitation and detection side by side.

title: Hacking the Cloud
summary: Nick Frichette's encyclopedia of offensive cloud techniques with concrete commands you can run. A practical companion to the cloud CTFs.

title: CloudGoat
summary: Rhino Security Labs' 'vulnerable by design' AWS deployment with around 20 Terraform scenarios, from IAM privilege escalation to EC2 SSRF through IMDS. Deploys vulnerable infrastructure you can practice on.

title: Prowler
summary: The most popular open-source multi-cloud security scanner, covering AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, and Microsoft 365 against CIS, NIST, and PCI-DSS benchmarks.

title: ScoutSuite
summary: NCC Group's read-only multi-cloud auditor. It enumerates your cloud and produces an interactive HTML report of misconfigurations.

title: Pacu
summary: Described as the Metasploit of AWS: an open-source AWS exploitation framework for IAM privilege escalation, backdoors, and Lambda attacks.

title: Stratus Red Team
summary: Datadog's granular cloud adversary emulation, described as Atomic Red Team for the cloud. Attack techniques are mapped to MITRE ATT&CK across AWS, Azure, GCP, Entra, and Kubernetes.

title: AWS Certified Security - Specialty (SCS-C03)
summary: The industry-recognized AWS cloud security credential: 65 questions in 170 minutes.

title: AZ-500 Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate
summary: The official Azure security credential. Note: 2026 Microsoft sources report AZ-500 is being retired and replaced by SC-500, so confirm its status on Microsoft Learn before booking.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025)
summary: The canonical risk list for LLM apps, from prompt injection (LLM01) to unbounded consumption (LLM10), using the 2025 reorganization.

title: PortSwigger Web LLM Attacks
summary: Eight free hands-on labs from the Burp makers covering excessive agency, LLM API exploitation, indirect prompt injection, insecure output handling, and AI agent abuse.

title: Gandalf by Lakera
summary: A prompt-injection game where you trick an AI defender into revealing secret passwords across increasingly hardened levels. An agentic variant exists too.

title: Garak
summary: NVIDIA's maintained LLM vulnerability scanner, a red-teaming and assessment toolkit for generative AI. Stable release 0.17.0 landed September 2026.

title: Promptfoo
summary: Declarative YAML-based LLM red-teaming and evals with OWASP LLM Top 10 probes you can run in CI. Open-source under the MIT license.

title: PyRIT
summary: Microsoft's Python Risk Identification Tool: an automation framework for red-teaming generative AI, used in Microsoft's own AI Red Team training.

title: Simon Willison's blog (prompt injection)
summary: The September 2022 post that coined the term 'prompt injection', with a helpful SQL-injection analogy. His 'lethal trifecta' piece is a good follow-up read.

title: OWASP AI Security and Privacy Guide (AI Exchange)
summary: Over 200 pages of AI threats and controls aligned to international standards. An OWASP flagship project, now called AI Exchange.

title: Anthropic Research - Many-Shot Jailbreaking
summary: Frontier-lab research on the classic long-context jailbreak technique, and a natural entry point into Anthropic's alignment and security research.

title: Google DeepMind - Securing the future of AI agents
summary: DeepMind's June 2026 AI control roadmap: defending internal systems against misaligned agents through monitoring coverage and red-team exercises.

title: Lakera blog - 'Stop Letting Models Grade Their Own Homework'
summary: Vendor research arguing that LLM-as-judge setups fail at prompt-injection defense, and that guardrails need layering. Treat the vendor angle skeptically and validate the claims yourself.

title: Pluralsight - LLM Prompt Injection: Attacks and Defenses
summary: A one-hour, seven-minute course by Gavin Johnson-Lynn on securing LLM applications and testing them for weaknesses.

title: LetsDefend
summary: A simulated SOC with a real alert queue: phishing, malware, and network alerts in a Tier-1 triage workflow. Acquired by Hack The Box in September 2025.

title: Blue Team Labs Online
summary: Over 250 DFIR and SOC investigations covering memory dumps, packet captures, and logs. The free BTJA pathway (about six to seven hours) is the standard starting lane.

title: CyberDefenders
summary: Dozens of free artifact-based blue-team CTFs in DFIR, threat hunting, and malware analysis. You get real artifacts and investigative questions to work through.

title: Security Blue Team - BTL1
summary: Often called the OSCP of blue team: a 24-hour hands-on lab exam covering phishing, forensics, threat intelligence, SIEM, and incident response, with one free resit within 12 months.

title: Security Blue Team - BTL2
summary: Advanced security operations: malware analysis, threat hunting, vulnerability management, and advanced SIEM. A free demo course is available to preview it.

title: MITRE ATT&CK
summary: The universal language of adversary behavior: 14 Enterprise tactics and their techniques and sub-techniques. Pair it with the ATT&CK Navigator for coverage mapping.

title: Splunk BOTS (Boss of the SOC)
summary: Splunk's official blue-team competition and the best free way to practice SPL on real attack data. The version 1 to 3 datasets are public.

title: Wazuh
summary: The leading open-source SIEM plus XDR: manager, agents, rules engine, file integrity monitoring, vulnerability detection, and active response. The default homelab SOC stack.

title: Velociraptor
summary: Rapid7's open-source endpoint DFIR and hunting framework: fleet-wide VQL hunts and live evidence collection.

title: Sigma rules repository
summary: Over 3,000 vendor-agnostic detection rules. Sigma does for logs what Snort does for network traffic and YARA does for files, and it is a core detection-as-code skill.

title: John Hammond (YouTube)
summary: Malware analysis, CTF and DFIR walkthroughs, and tool demos from a Principal Security Researcher at Huntress, with over 500,000 subscribers.

title: SANS DFIR Posters
summary: Free printable references: Hunt Evil, Windows Forensic Analysis, memory forensics, and intrusion discovery. Pin them above your desk.

title: SANS Internet Storm Center
summary: Daily practitioner threat diaries from about 40 volunteer handlers, plus the StormCast daily podcast. A habit worth building early.

title: The DFIR Report
summary: Real incident investigation write-ups with IOCs and ATT&CK mappings. Every report ships with Sigma rules you can use.

title: OSINT Framework
summary: An interactive tree categorizing thousands of free OSINT tools by use case: usernames, email, domains, images, dark web. The recon cheat sheet of the field.

title: Trace Labs Search Party CTF
summary: A nonprofit crowdsourced missing-persons OSINT CTF that works real cases for law enforcement, with up to four-person teams. The June 2026 global CTF was confirmed active.

title: Sherlock
summary: The standard username hunter across more than 400 platforms, the usual first pass for mapping a handle's digital footprint.

title: WhatsMyName
summary: A web tool powered by a community-curated dataset of 700+ sites. No install needed, and it complements Sherlock well.

title: theHarvester
summary: The classic passive email, subdomain, and host harvester for a target domain, drawing on search engines, DNS, certificate transparency, and LinkedIn.

title: Epieos
summary: Reverse email and phone lookup that reveals linked Google account data, registered services, and Maps reviews. One of the most-used email OSINT tools.

title: OSINT Techniques (Michael Bazzell)
summary: The definitive OSINT reference by a former FBI cyber-crimes task force investigator, updated almost yearly and used as a training manual by agencies.

title: Ghidra
summary: The NSA's free multi-architecture disassembler and decompiler with a genuinely competitive decompiler. Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: IDA Free
summary: The industry-standard disassembler. The free edition now bundles a cloud decompiler for students.

title: x64dbg
summary: The best free open-source debugger for Windows malware, and an intuitive dynamic-analysis complement to Ghidra.

title: Binary Ninja
summary: Fast IL-based analysis with a modern API. A free in-browser version lets students try the decompiler on small binaries immediately.

cost.price: Non-Commercial $299 / Commercial $1,199; 75% student discount ($74/$299); free in-browser version for small binaries

title: Cutter
summary: A friendly Qt GUI over rizin and radare2 that lowers the CLI learning curve for static analysis.

title: Detect It Easy (DIE)
summary: Identifies packers, compilers, and protectors in seconds. The first step before unpacking any sample.

title: Practical Malware Analysis (Sikorski & Honig, No Starch, 2012, 800 pp)
summary: The field's standard hands-on textbook; its lab exercises map directly to a reverse-engineering course syllabus.

title: Practical Binary Analysis (Dennis Andriesse, No Starch, 2018, 456 pp)
summary: Practical modern binary-analysis techniques with an ELF focus: the natural sequel to Practical Malware Analysis.

title: TCM Security: Practical Malware Analysis & Triage
summary: A structured video course by Matt Kiely (HuskyHacks) with labs. The cheapest structured paid malware-analysis training path.

title: 0ffset Training (formerly Zero2Automated)
summary: One-time-payment malware-analysis courses with a certification included. Good value compared to subscriptions.

cost.price: Standard £149.99 one-time; Ultimate Bundle £185.99, includes certification

title: OALABS
summary: Free practical malware-analysis walkthroughs on unpacking and config extraction, with a companion research wiki.

title: MalwareAnalysisForHedgehogs
summary: Gentle, practical analysis videos, ideal for a student's very first malware sample.

title: crackmes.one
summary: A huge free archive of graded reverse-engineering challenges. The perfect practice library for RE.

title: Flare-On (Mandiant / Google)
summary: The annual flagship RE CTF from Mandiant, with excellent public writeups. A benchmark challenge set for serious students.

title: Autopsy
summary: The standard free forensic suite: a GUI over the Sleuth Kit used by law enforcement, with timelines, keyword search, and carving built in.

title: The Sleuth Kit (TSK)
summary: The core CLI toolkit: fls, mmls, fsstat, icat. Learning it teaches the actual forensic primitives behind Autopsy.

title: Eric Zimmerman's EZ Tools
summary: The global standard for Windows artifact parsing: MFT, prefetch, registry, shellbags. Single-author tools used worldwide.

title: KAPE (Kroll Artifact Parser & Extractor)
summary: The standard for rapid Windows triage: it collects and parses artifacts in minutes.

cost.priceNote: Free for students, law enforcement, and researchers; commercial engagements require a license

title: 13Cubed (Richard Davis)
summary: The best free Windows DFIR video courses, including a 12-part Memory Forensics and a 22-part Windows Forensics playlist.

title: DFIRScience
summary: Clear DFIR workflow walkthroughs, from evidence to timeline.

title: The DFIR Report (YouTube)
summary: Real-intrusion case walkthroughs showing how actual incident response teams investigate.

title: SANS DFIR
summary: Free SANS summit talks and a DFIR resource hub from the industry's top training body.

title: MemLabs
summary: A dedicated memory-forensics CTF set that pairs perfectly with Volatility 3.

title: File System Forensic Analysis (Brian Carrier, Addison-Wesley, 2005, 600 pp)
summary: The definitive reference on file-system internals, written by the author of the Sleuth Kit.

title: Volatility 3
summary: The standard memory-forensics framework, rewritten for modern memory formats.

title: CryptoHack
summary: Twelve categories and five structured courses: the best hands-on introduction to attacking real cryptography.

title: Cryptopals (Matasano)
summary: Forty-eight exercises built from real-world crypto failures. The classic crypto programmer's workout.

title: CryptoPals Guided Tour (Eli Sohl)
summary: Challenge-by-challenge video walkthroughs of Cryptopals, for when you get stuck.

title: Cryptography I (Dan Boneh, Stanford / Coursera)
summary: The rigorous university crypto course, from number theory to zero knowledge, with a free graduate textbook alongside it.

title: Serious Cryptography (Jean-Philippe Aumasson, No Starch, 2nd ed. 2024)
summary: Modern, practical crypto engineering (TLS, post-quantum, zero knowledge) by an applied cryptographer. The 2nd edition is current.

title: Understanding Cryptography (Christof Paar & Jan Pelzl)
summary: The applied crypto textbook that explains the math step by step with minimal prerequisites, plus about 24 free lectures on YouTube.

title: CyberChef
summary: The 'cyber Swiss Army knife' from GCHQ. Runs fully in the browser and is indispensable for CTF crypto and encoding work.

title: Handbook of Applied Cryptography
summary: The free encyclopedic crypto reference. It deepens any topic the courses touch lightly.

title: PicoCTF (CMU) - Crypto Category
summary: A year-round free CTF with a crypto category. Note: 2026 reports suggest picoCTF is folding into the CyLab Security Academy, so verify before linking.

title: pwn.college
summary: A fully modular pwn and RE curriculum from first principles, from Arizona State University. The closest thing to a free degree module in exploitation.

title: Nightmare (guyinatuxedo)
summary: Over 90 binary-exploitation challenges with documented writeups, all solvable with open-source tools.

title: ROP Emporium
summary: A focused ROP practice ladder from 32-bit to 64-bit. The standard ROP drill set.

title: MBE - Modern Binary Exploitation (RPISEC)
summary: University course materials with VM labs covering modern exploitation end to end.

title: exploit.education
summary: The classic exploit-development VMs (Protostar, Phoenix, Nebula) teaching primitives step by step.

title: LiveOverflow
summary: The best binary-exploitation theory series on YouTube. Builds the 'why' behind each technique.

title: pwnable.kr
summary: The classic pwn wargame, graded from a baby's first stack overflow upward.

title: Hacking: The Art of Exploitation (Jon Erickson, No Starch 2nd ed. 2008, 488 pp)
summary: The beloved hands-on exploit primer with its own liveCD lab environment. Unbeatable value used.

title: Corelan exploit-writing tutorials
summary: The classic Windows exploit-writing tutorial series that every exploit developer has read.

title: Azeria Labs
summary: The standard ARM assembly and ARM exploitation reference. Fills the non-x86 gap.

summary: Makes GDB usable for exploit development: ROP search, heap inspection, context display. The pwn.college workflow standard.

title: Caido
summary: A fast, modern Burp alternative with AI plugins.

summary: The free open-source scanner from OWASP. An ideal first DAST tool.

title: Nuclei
summary: A template-based vulnerability scanner with a huge community template library.

title: OWASP Juice Shop
summary: OWASP's flagship modern vulnerable application (MIT license): a realistic shop to practice real vulnerabilities in.

title: DVWA

title: OWASP WebGoat
summary: OWASP's insecure Java app with guided lessons per vulnerability class.

title: OWASP Top 10
summary: The industry-standard web risk list. The 2025 edition is current.

title: HackTricks
summary: A massive pentest and CTF methodology wiki, actively maintained.

title: PayloadsAllTheThings
summary: The biggest payload and bypass collection per vulnerability class. You will open this daily.

summary: The 2026-edition filter-evasion vectors, tested against real browsers. Pairs with the Academy labs.

summary: The flagship hacking lab platform. Retired machines pair perfectly with IppSec walkthroughs.

title: IppSec

title: STÖK
summary: Bug bounty methodology and mindset from a multi-award hunter (Uber, Salesforce, US DoD).

summary: The web application security bible by Burp's creator. From 2011, but its fundamentals still hold.

title: Real-World Bug Hunting
summary: Real rewarded bug-bounty case studies from Twitter, Facebook, Google, and Uber. Learn from findings that actually got paid.

title: Nmap
summary: The network scanner everything else builds on. Essential for discovery and enumeration.

title: Wireshark
summary: The protocol analyzer (GPLv2), shipping TShark for CLI capture and analysis.

title: Metasploit Framework
summary: Rapid7's open-source exploitation framework, preinstalled on Kali.

title: Responder

title: BloodHound
summary: Graph-based Active Directory attack-path mapping by SpecterOps. Shows the paths attackers actually take.

title: SecLists
summary: The canonical wordlist collection for fuzzing and content discovery.

title: GTFOBins
summary: A reference of Unix binaries usable for privilege escalation and bypass.

title: LOLBAS
summary: The Windows living-off-the-land binaries reference for post-exploitation.

title: Metasploit Unleashed
summary: OffSec's free Metasploit course with no registration. The official starting point.

title: Nmap Network Scanning
summary: Written by Nmap's author, Fyodor. The 9th edition (August 2025) is current, and more than half the book is free at nmap.org/book.

title: TCM Security Practical Ethical Hacking
summary: A full beginner-to-pentester video course covering networking, Active Directory, and web basics.

title: Darknet Diaries
summary: Narrative real-hack stories by Jack Rhysider. Builds security intuition better than any textbook.

title: Professor Messer Network+
summary: A free exam-mapped video course for the current N10-009 Network+ cycle.

summary: Cisco's network simulator. Sufficient for all CCNA-level practice.

title: GNS3

title: SubnettingPractice.com
summary: Free interactive subnetting drills. Subnetting is free marks on exams.

title: Chris Greer (Practical Networking)
summary: Wireshark and TCP/IP packet analysis made approachable, with 140K+ subscribers.

title: NetworkLessons.com
summary: 820 lessons and 100+ hours of video for CCNA, CCNP, and CCIE, with a $1 seven-day trial.

title: TCP/IP Illustrated, Vol 1
summary: The definitive protocol reference, endorsed by Vint Cerf.

summary: The standard university networking textbook. The 9th edition (2025) covers HTTP/3, QUIC, Wi-Fi 6, and 5G.

summary: The baseline certification that still opens doors. Every employer recognizes it, and it teaches core security vocabulary.

title: EC-Council CEH v13
summary: Heavy on theory and tool names. Useful when a job posting or HR filter asks for it by name.

title: INE eJPT

title: INE eCPPT
summary: A 24-hour practical exam that tests real pentest methodology. A solid step up from eJPT.

title: TCM Security PJPT
summary: The exam spans two days plus two for the report, the certification never expires, and training is included in the price. Confirmed on the official TCM FAQ, October 2026.

summary: A five-day practical network pentest plus a live debrief. One of the best-value professional certs, and it never expires.

summary: The gold standard pentest certification. The brutal 24-hour exam teaches real persistence and enumeration.

title: ISC2 CISSP

title: CompTIA PenTest+ (PT0-003)
summary: A good structured path between Security+ and OSCP, covering pentest planning, tools, and reporting.

title: Zero-Point Security CRTO
summary: A 48-hour red-team ops exam built around Cobalt Strike. The respected certification for real-world operator tradecraft.

title: GIAC GSEC
summary: Vendor-neutral security fundamentals with hands-on CyberLive questions, valid four years and widely respected.

title: HTB CPTS (Certified Penetration Testing Specialist)
summary: Rapidly gaining industry respect. An exam-based certification from the HTB Academy track.

summary: The industry standard for mobile app security requirements, organized into clear control groups from storage to privacy.

summary: The standard Dex-to-Java decompiler for turning Android APKs back into readable code.

title: Trivy
summary: One scanner for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and secrets across containers, infrastructure as code, and SBOMs.

title: Gitleaks
summary: The go-to secrets scanner for git repositories. Note the project is feature-complete and now receives security patches only.

summary: A vulnerability management hub that imports results from more than 150 scanners into one trackable dashboard.

title: Checkov

title: Snyk
summary: Developer-friendly scanning for code, containers, and IaC, with direct GitHub, GitLab, and IDE integrations.

title: pwntools
summary: The standard Python library for exploit development and CTF scripting: tubes, packing, shellcraft, and ROP helpers in one package.

title: Reverse Engineering for Beginners (Dennis Yurichev)
summary: A huge free book that teaches x86 and ARM assembly and reverse engineering from zero, with real examples throughout.

cost.priceNote: Free PDF download; printed editions sold separately

title: dCode
summary: Over 900 small tools for classical ciphers, encodings, and code identification. Paste the blob, figure out what it is, decode it.

title: WeChall
summary: A global scoreboard that links your accounts across challenge sites and ranks you on all of them in one profile. Teams check it when recruiting.
The free federal guide that defines the whole forensic process: collection, examination, analysis, and reporting. Dense but it is the reference every serious analyst reads first.
title: NIST SP 800-86: Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response

summary: Dozens of free pcap exercises with full walkthroughs, built by Brad Duncan. Download the capture, find the infection, then check your answer against his.
title: Malware-Traffic-Analysis.net Exercises

cost.priceNote: Retail paperback around $50; used copies widely available for much less.

summary: Written by the Volatility team itself. Over 900 pages on Windows, Linux, and Mac memory forensics with exercises per chapter. The book analysts keep on their desk.
title: The Art of Memory Forensics

summary: A free, MIT-licensed incident investigation report template with section-by-section writing guidance and a browser viewer that renders your draft into a clean PDF.
title: Incident Report Template (Antti Kurittu)

cost.priceNote: Exam fee; SANS training course is extra.

summary: The certification for working incident investigators: memory forensics, timeline analysis, threat hunting, and APT intrusions, with hands-on CyberLive tasks.
title: GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA)

summary: The maintained successor to CrackMapExec. Tests one credential against a whole subnet over SMB, LDAP, WinRM and more: enumerate shares, users and sessions, spray passwords, dump SAM and LSA, run post-exploitation modules.
title: NetExec

summary: Tenable's free vulnerability scanner for non-commercial use: scans up to 5 IPs with the same plugin engine as Nessus Professional. Verified students can get Essentials Plus (20 IPs) free for a year.
title: Tenable Nessus Essentials

summary: Intentionally vulnerable Ubuntu VM built for practicing network exploitation. Pair it with Metasploit: scan it, enumerate it, and work through real exploits against real services in your own lab.
title: Metasploitable 2

summary: Modern pivoting tool that builds a full TUN tunnel back through a compromised host, so tools like Nmap run directly against the internal network. No SOCKS, no proxychains needed on your side.
title: Ligolo-ng

summary: Fast TCP and UDP tunnel over HTTP. Single binary, client and server. The simple way to forward ports and build SOCKS proxies through a compromised host when you need something lighter than a full tunnel.
title: Chisel

summary: A curated collection of real penetration test reports published by consulting firms. Read them before you write your first report: structure, tone, severity ratings, and how findings are explained to non-technical readers.
title: Public Pentesting Reports

summary: Every Nmap flag you will actually use, grouped by task: host discovery, scan types, version detection, NSE scripts, evasion, and output. Updated for 2026 with a downloadable PDF.
title: StationX Nmap Cheat Sheet

summary: Turns an SSH connection into a transparent VPN to the remote network. No admin rights needed on the remote side. The fastest way to pivot when all you have is SSH access to one box.
title: sshuttle

summary: OffSec's curated collection of real Google dorks, sorted by category: exposed files, login portals, vulnerable servers, and more. The reference for learning advanced search operators, and each dork shows you what a working query looks like.
title: Google Hacking Database

summary: Sectigo's free Certificate Transparency search. Query any domain and see every certificate ever issued for it, which reveals subdomains you would never find by guessing. Querying it is fully passive; you never touch the target.
title: crt.sh

summary: Troy Hunt's free breach-checking service. Enter an email or domain and see every public breach it appears in, with per-breach details on what data leaked. Free for manual lookups; the API needs a paid key.
title: Have I Been Pwned

summary: Free open-source investigation guides from the team that set the standard for modern OSINT: verification, geolocation, social media research, and evidence preservation. Written from real investigations, not theory.
title: Bellingcat Resources and Toolkits

cost.priceNote: Free accounts get limited search credits; full API access and exports need a paid plan.

summary: The search engine for the internet's connected devices. Find exposed services, open databases, and misconfigured servers by banner, port, and product, without scanning anything yourself.
title: Shodan

summary: The Internet Archive's record of the web. Pull deleted pages, old site versions, and files that targets thought were gone; essential whenever current recon comes up empty.
title: Wayback Machine

summary: Xeno Kovah's free full-length x86 assembly course: 234 slides, 12 hours of video, and the CMU binary bomb lab. Old material, but the fundamentals have not changed.
title: Open Security Training: Intro to x86

summary: Type C code and watch the compiler turn it into assembly in real time. The fastest way to build the C-to-assembly mental map that static analysis runs on.
title: Compiler Explorer (Godbolt)

summary: Mandiant's installer that turns a clean Windows VM into a malware analysis box in one script: debuggers, disassemblers, and utilities all installed for you.
title: FLARE-VM

summary: Lenny Zeltzer's Linux toolkit for malware analysts: a ready-made VM or Docker images with hundreds of free analysis tools preinstalled.
title: REMnux

cost.priceNote: Community tier is free but every analysis you run is public. Paid tiers add private analyses and longer sessions.

summary: Interactive malware sandbox: you drive a real VM in your browser, click through the infection, and watch processes, network, and registry activity in real time.
title: ANY.RUN

summary: Free automated unpacker from the OALABS team. Upload a packed sample, get the unpacked payloads back. The first stop before you unpack a packer by hand.
title: UnpacMe

summary: The largest public malware sample and research-paper archive. The papers and family writeups are a goldmine once you can read assembly.
title: VX-Underground

cost.priceNote: Exam fee; SANS FOR610 training course is extra.

summary: The recognized certification for malware analysts: behavioral analysis, Windows assembly, packed and .NET malware, malicious documents, with hands-on CyberLive tasks.
title: GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM)
Security Certification Roadmap (Paul Jerimy)
summary: A visual map of nearly every security certification, arranged by specialty and level. The fastest way to see which cert belongs to which career track before you spend money.

cost.priceNote: Free online; printed poster versions sold via print-on-demand

title: Professor Messer Security+ SY0-701 Course
summary: 121 free videos, about 15 hours, covering every Security+ exam objective in order. The standard free prep for the exam; his site also sells notes and practice exams.

cost.priceNote: All videos free; course notes and practice exams are paid

title: freeCodeCamp Information Security
summary: Free interactive certificate course covering network security, cryptography, and secure app development with hands-on labs. A solid zero-to-certified path for beginners before touching paid platforms.

title: Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate
summary: Google's 8-course entry-level program on Coursera covering Linux, SQL, SIEM tools, Python automation, and incident response. All content is free to audit; the certificate itself is paid with financial aid available.

title: Cybrary
summary: Cybersecurity training platform with structured career paths (SOC analyst, pentester) plus free courses. Good for students who want a guided curriculum with cert-aligned content.

title: Fortinet NSE Training Institute
summary: Fortinet's own training: NSE levels 1 through 3 are free and teach network security fundamentals, firewalls, and threat concepts. Useful free cert badges for a student CV.

title: Open Security Training 2
summary: University-grade open course material on reverse engineering, malware analysis, and architecture internals. Hard but free; the closest thing to a degree-level RE curriculum online.

title: Cisco Skills for All
summary: Cisco's free learning platform with courses from intro-to-cybersecurity up to networking essentials, each earning a verifiable digital badge. Good first credentials for beginners.

title: TCM Security Academy
summary: Practical, no-fluff pentest training by The Cyber Mentor team; several entry courses are free and the paid tracks stay cheap. Known for clear teaching and OSCP-relevant material.

title: INE Security
summary: Professional training platform behind the eJPT and eCPPT certifications, with a free starter tier. Worth it once you outgrow beginner courses and want cert-grade depth.

title: YesWeHack Dojo
summary: YesWeHack's free training dojo with guided bug-bounty labs and tutorials. A natural stepping stone into the YesWeHack platform for aspiring bug bounty hunters.

title: SANS Holiday Hack Challenge
summary: SANS's free annual December CTF with a story-driven challenge series spanning web, forensics, and crypto. One of the best free yearly events to test everything you learned.

title: MITRE D3FEND
summary: MITRE's knowledge graph of defensive countermeasures mapped against ATT&CK techniques. Use it to learn what a detection actually looks like on the blue side.

title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
summary: The US government's live list of vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild, with required remediation dates. Essential for prioritizing what to patch and what to learn to exploit.

title: National Vulnerability Database (NVD)
summary: NIST's official CVE database with severity scores, descriptions, and references. The first place to check details of any CVE you encounter.

title: Exploit Database
summary: OffSec's archive of public exploits and proof-of-concepts, searchable by CVE and product. Pair it with the NVD to go from vulnerability description to working exploit.

title: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
summary: The community standard for how to test web applications, technique by technique with concrete test cases. Required reading before any serious web pentest or bug bounty work.

title: roadmap.sh Cyber Security
summary: An interactive, community-maintained roadmap of the entire cyber career path with checkboxes and resource links. Useful to see where you stand and what comes next.

title: OffSec Proving Grounds
summary: OffSec's practice lab with a free tier of machines rated for OSCP-prep difficulty. Good middle ground between free CTF boxes and the paid OSCP labs.

title: HackMyVM
summary: Free community platform with downloadable vulnerable VMs and browser challenges across web, Linux, and Windows. Less famous than HackTheBox but genuinely free.

title: VulnMachines
summary: Free vulnerable machines to download and practice pentesting on your own hardware. A simple way to build a local lab without any subscription.

title: CyberSecLabs
summary: UK-based lab platform with free and premium machines for practicing pentest skills in realistic scenarios. A smaller, beginner-friendly alternative to the big lab platforms.

title: OWASP Mutillidae II
summary: Deliberately vulnerable web app with 40+ challenges covering the OWASP Top Ten, with hints built in. One of the easiest first targets for practicing web attacks locally.

title: Google Gruyere
summary: Google's cheesy (their words) vulnerable web app with guided exercises on XSS, CSRF, and session bugs. Short, free, and teaches the fundamentals well.

title: Atomic Red Team
summary: Red Canary's library of small, scriptable ATT&CK-mapped tests for validating your own detections. Run the attacks, then write Sigma rules to catch them.

title: Splunk Attack Range
summary: Builds vulnerable local or cloud environments and collects attack telemetry into Splunk. Lets blue-team students practice on logs from attacks they generated themselves.

title: Security Onion
summary: Free Linux distro bundling Zeek, Suricata, ELK, and full packet capture for security monitoring and threat hunting. The fastest way to build a home SOC.

title: Commando VM
summary: Mandiant's Windows pentesting VM, sibling to FLARE-VM, packed with offensive tools. A clean starting point for Windows-side testing without hunting down installers.

title: SANS SIFT Workstation
summary: SANS's free Ubuntu-based forensics workstation with a full incident-response toolkit. The standard free environment for learning disk and memory forensics.

title: Kali Linux
summary: The industry-standard pentest distro with hundreds of security tools preinstalled. Every offensive student should know it; start with the official download page.

title: Metasploitable 3
summary: Rapid7's intentionally vulnerable VMs (Linux and Windows) built for practicing exploitation with Metasploit. A classic first target for learning the exploit workflow.

title: HackTheBox Sherlocks
summary: HTB's blue-team investigations: downloadable forensic scenarios where you answer questions from logs, disk images, and pcaps. Some content free, full access with subscription.

title: TryHackMe Advent of Cyber
summary: TryHackMe's free yearly December event with a daily beginner-friendly security challenge behind an advent calendar. A fun low-pressure way to build a daily habit.

title: National Cyber League
summary: US collegiate cybersecurity competition with individual and team seasons covering nine skill domains. Good competitive experience if your school fields a team.

title: HackThisSite
summary: One of the oldest hacking challenge sites, with realistic missions spanning web, crypto, and forensics. Dated look, still solid fundamentals practice.

title: pwnable.tw
summary: Taiwanese binary-exploitation wargame with 30 progressively harder pwn challenges. A respected rite of passage for exploit developers.

title: pwnable.xyz
summary: Modern binary-exploitation wargame with 80 challenges covering classic and newer techniques. Good next step after pwnable.kr.

title: RingZer0 CTF
summary: Long-running CTF site with hundreds of challenges across crypto, web, reversing, and steganography. Deep catalog for grinding a specific category.

title: XSS Game
summary: Google's six-level game teaching you to find and exploit XSS bugs, then fix them. Takes an hour and makes reflected vs stored XSS click.

title: OWASP WrongSecrets
summary: Deliberately insecure app teaching secrets management: find hardcoded keys across Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud configs. Fills a gap most web labs ignore.

title: NahamSec
summary: Ben Sadeghipour's bug-bounty channel with real recon and hacking streams. Shows how working hunters actually find bugs.

title: InsiderPhD
summary: Katie Paxton's channel on bug bounty methodology and breaking into security careers. Clear, beginner-friendly explanations.

title: TCM Security Academy
summary: The Cyber Mentor team's free YouTube courses, including full ethical-hacking and OSINT series. High-quality teaching, zero cost.

title: Simply Cyber
summary: Gerald Auger's career-focused channel with daily threat intel and certification guidance. Good for staying oriented as a newcomer.

title: David Bombal
summary: Huge networking and ethical-hacking library with expert interviews and tool demos. Start with his networking playlists.

title: Tib3rius
summary: Web-hacking walkthroughs and privilege-escalation courses from a working pentester. Practical, no-nonsense teaching style.

title: MalwareTech
summary: Marcus Hutchins' deep dives into malware techniques and botnet takedowns. Advanced material from someone who has dismantled real malware at scale.

title: Black Hills InfoSec
summary: Webcasts and talks from a respected pentest firm on red-team tradecraft and AD attacks. Professional-grade content, free.

title: HackerSploit
summary: Alexis Ahmed's beginner-friendly Linux, networking, and ethical-hacking series. One of the best starting points for total newcomers.

title: Black Hat
summary: Official Black Hat conference talks on cutting-edge research. Watch to see where the industry's best minds are focused.

title: DEF CON
summary: Official DEF CON talks from the world's largest hacker conference. Raw, deep, and occasionally wild research presentations.

title: Hak5
summary: Darren Kitchen's long-running show on hacking gear, Wi-Fi attacks, and payloads. Entertaining and hands-on.

title: Trail of Bits Blog
summary: Deep technical posts from one of the best security research firms, on cryptography, compilers, and tooling. Dense but worth the effort.

title: The Hacker News
summary: High-volume daily feed of breaches, vulnerabilities, and threat campaigns. The fastest way to keep up with security news.

title: BleepingComputer
summary: Timely reporting on ransomware, malware, and vulnerabilities with practical remediation advice. A staple bookmark for any practitioner.

title: WeLiveSecurity
summary: ESET's research blog with quality malware analysis and threat reports. Good source of real-world case studies.

title: Schneier on Security
summary: Bruce Schneier's long-running commentary on security, privacy, and policy. Sharp thinking that trains your judgment, not just your tools.

title: Dark Reading
summary: Enterprise security news and analysis aimed at practitioners. Good for understanding how security decisions get made in industry.

title: SecurityWeek
summary: Cybersecurity business and threat news with solid vulnerability coverage. Useful for tracking industry trends.

title: Troy Hunt
summary: Creator of Have I Been Pwned writes about breaches, web security fails, and password culture. Entertaining and educational in equal measure.

title: Project Zero
summary: Google's elite vulnerability research team's writeups on zero-days they found and reported. The gold standard for exploit writeups; migrated off Blogspot to its own domain in 2025.

title: Rhino Security Labs Blog
summary: Pentest firm's research on AWS attacks, web vulnerabilities, and red-team techniques. Practical posts with real engagement stories.

title: ExamCompass
summary: Free practice exams for CompTIA, Cisco, and other IT certifications with detailed explanations. Good for drilling Security+ style questions.

title: Crucial Exams
summary: Free certification practice tests with a paid premium tier ($19.99/month) for extra features. Useful question bank for Security+ and Network+ prep.

title: Burp Suite Certified Practitioner
summary: PortSwigger's own web-security certification: a practical exam built on their free academy labs. Cheap, respected, and proves real web-hacking skill.

title: OffSec OSWE (WEB-300)
summary: OffSec's advanced web exploitation course and exam focused on white-box code review and custom exploits. For students serious about web pentest careers.

cost.priceNote: course plus one exam attempt, 90 days

title: OffSec OSEP (PEN-300)
summary: OffSec's evasion-focused pentest course teaching AV bypass and advanced AD attacks. A natural follow-up after OSCP for red-team aspirants.

title: GIAC GPEN
summary: GIAC's pentester certification covering methodology, password attacks, and web app testing. Well-regarded in enterprise and government roles.

title: GIAC GCIH
summary: GIAC's incident-handler cert on detection, response, and common attack techniques. Strong credential for SOC and DFIR career paths.

title: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
summary: ISC2's entry-level certification covering security principles and risk management. The free One Million program ended May 2026; the exam now costs $199.

title: CompTIA CySA+ (CS0-003)
summary: CompTIA's analyst-level cert on threat detection, vulnerability management, and incident response. A solid blue-team counterpart to Security+.

title: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009)
summary: CompTIA's vendor-neutral networking certification (current version N10-009). The networking foundation most cyber roles quietly expect.

title: SANS NewsBites
summary: SANS's twice-weekly executive summary of the most important security news. A quick way to stay current without doomscrolling.

title: The Many Hats Club
summary: Large, welcoming infosec Discord community with channels for every specialty and career stage. Good place to ask beginner questions without judgment.

title: r/netsec
summary: Reddit's technical security community sharing research, writeups, and tools. High signal-to-noise for staying current on real research.

title: r/AskNetsec
summary: Reddit's Q&A community for security career and study questions. Useful for honest answers about certs, jobs, and learning paths.

title: Malicious Life
summary: Cybereason-produced podcast telling the stories behind major hacks and malware. Great for building intuition about how real attacks unfold.

title: GreyNoise
summary: Tells you whether an IP scanning you is a known benign scanner or a real threat. Invaluable context for SOC analysts triaging alerts.

title: VirusTotal
summary: Google's multi-engine scanner for files, URLs, and hashes with community intelligence. First stop for checking if something is malicious.

title: urlscan.io
summary: Free service that scans URLs and shows screenshots, DOM, and network activity. Great for safely inspecting phishing links.

title: MalwareBazaar
summary: abuse.ch's free malware sample repository for researchers. Download real samples for analysis in your lab.

title: URLhaus
summary: abuse.ch's database of malicious URLs distributing malware. Feed it into your defenses or study live phishing infrastructure.

title: ThreatFox
summary: abuse.ch's indicator-of-compromise database with context on malware families. Solid free threat-intel feed for SOC work.

title: AbuseIPDB
summary: Community-reported database of abusive IP addresses with reputation scores. Quick check during incident triage.

title: AlienVault OTX
summary: AT&T's open threat-intelligence sharing community with pulses on active campaigns. Free to join and contribute.

title: Subfinder
summary: ProjectDiscovery's fast subdomain enumeration tool, a staple of bug-bounty recon. Simple, fast, and scriptable.

title: Hybrid Analysis
summary: Free online malware sandbox with detailed behavioral reports. Detonate suspicious files without building your own lab.

title: Zeek
summary: Powerful network analysis framework that turns traffic into structured logs. The backbone of many SOC detection pipelines.

title: Suricata
summary: Open-source IDS/IPS and network security monitoring engine. Learn to write rules here and you understand detection.

title: Assetnote Wordlists
summary: Curated, high-quality wordlists for content discovery, maintained by Assetnote. Better hit rates than generic lists for directory fuzzing.

title: FuzzDB
summary: Community dictionary of attack payloads for fuzzing: XSS, SQLi, LFI patterns and more. Plug it into Burp Intruder or ffuf.

title: tcpdump
summary: The classic command-line packet analyzer. Learn its filters and you can capture exactly the traffic you need anywhere.

title: Censys
summary: Internet-wide scan data searchable by certificate, banner, and protocol. Like Shodan with a research-grade dataset; free tier available.

title: Corsy
summary: Scans a domain for CORS misconfigurations such as overly permissive origins. Fast triage check every web pentester runs before manual testing.

title: WPScan
summary: WordPress vulnerability scanner that enumerates plugins, themes, users and known CVEs. Standard first step for any WordPress target; the free API tier covers casual use.
priceNote: Free API tier: 25 vulnerability database requests/day; commercial API for heavier use.

title: Nikto
summary: Long-running open-source web server scanner checking 6,700+ dangerous files, outdated software and misconfigurations. Noisy but thorough; good for quick baseline audits of a web server.

title: XSStrike
summary: Context-aware XSS fuzzer that analyzes responses to craft working payloads instead of blindly spraying strings. Includes a built-in crawler and WAF detection; useful when manual XSS hunting stalls.

title: WhatWeb
summary: Fingerprints web servers, frameworks and plugins (1,700+ signatures) from HTTP headers and page content. The standard tech-stack identifier for a target before choosing exploits.

title: CMSeeK
summary: Detects 180+ CMS platforms and versions, then looks up known vulnerabilities for what it finds. Cuts CMS recon from manual guessing to a single run.

title: Arjun
summary: Discovers hidden HTTP GET/POST parameters by fuzzing a large wordlist against endpoints. Essential for finding unlinked parameters on APIs and web apps.

title: droopescan
summary: Scans Drupal, Silverstripe and other supported CMS for version, plugins and themes with known vulnerabilities. Focused alternative when broader scanners miss a Drupal install.

title: ParamSpider
summary: Mines URLs with parameters from the Wayback Machine and Common Crawl for a target domain. Feed its output to fuzzers; cheap way to find forgotten endpoints with juicy query strings.

title: gau (GetAllUrls)
summary: Fetches known URLs for a domain from AlienVault OTX, Common Crawl, URLScan and the Wayback Machine. Recon staple for mapping attack surface quickly.

title: waybackurls
summary: Pulls archived URLs for a domain from the Wayback Machine's CDX API. Quick source of old endpoints, files and parameters other tools may skip.

title: wafw00f
summary: Identifies which WAF or security product sits in front of a web application. Know the WAF before you burn payloads against it.

title: Retire.js
summary: Detects known-vulnerable JavaScript libraries in a web app, via scanner, browser extension or CLI. Fast check for outdated jQuery, Bootstrap and friends during app assessments.

title: Photon
summary: Crawler that extracts URLs, endpoints, secrets and files from a target site, with OSINT plugins. Good first pass for mapping a web app's hidden surface.

title: CRLFuzz
summary: Fuzzes for CRLF injection and HTTP response splitting vulnerabilities. Niche but real: one tool for a bug class most scanners ignore.

title: Wappalyzer
summary: Browser extension and API that identifies technologies on any website (CMS, frameworks, analytics). Instant tech-stack read of a target; the free browser add-on covers everyday use.
priceNote: Browser extension free; API plans paid.

title: httpx
summary: ProjectDiscovery's HTTP toolkit: probes live hosts, grabs titles, tech fingerprints and status codes at high speed. Pipeline glue between subdomain lists and deeper scanning.

title: katana
summary: ProjectDiscovery's fast crawler and spider for mapping URLs, JS files and endpoints of a target. Built for modern JS-heavy apps; feeds directly into nuclei and other PD tools.

title: Gobuster
summary: Go-based directory, DNS and vhost brute-forcer. Fast, stable and the baseline every student should learn before reaching for heavier fuzzers.

title: feroxbuster
summary: Recursive content discovery tool that auto-follows found directories. Preferred over gobuster for deeper directory enumeration thanks to recursion and smart filtering.

title: ffuf
summary: Very fast web fuzzer for directories, parameters, vhosts and more, with flexible filtering. The Swiss-army fuzzer for custom wordlist attacks.

title: dirsearch
summary: Python-based web path scanner with multi-threading and smart request handling. Popular choice for directory brute-forcing with good defaults.

title: DalFox
summary: Fast XSS scanner and parameter analyzer, rewritten in Rust (v3) for speed. Good automated XSS triage before manual verification.

title: sqlmap
summary: The definitive automated SQL injection exploitation tool: detection, database fingerprinting, data extraction. Learn it on labs like DVWA; know its limits before real engagements.

title: testssl.sh
summary: Checks TLS/SSL configuration for weak ciphers, protocols and known vulnerabilities from the command line. Standard tool for SSL audit tasks.

title: SSLyze
summary: Python library and CLI for analyzing TLS configuration of servers. Scriptable alternative to testssl.sh when you need TLS checks inside automation.

title: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
summary: Concise, peer-reviewed guidance on authentication, XSS prevention, crypto storage and dozens of other topics. The first bookmark for secure coding and review work.

title: Nuclei Templates
summary: Community repository of 9,000+ vulnerability detection templates for the nuclei scanner. The detection library that makes nuclei powerful.

title: Amass
summary: OWASP's in-depth attack surface mapping: subdomain enum, DNS, graph-based relationship discovery. Slower but far more thorough than single-source tools.

title: Sublist3r
summary: Enumerates subdomains via search engines and certificate transparency. Lightweight classic; still useful as a second source alongside subfinder.

title: assetfinder
summary: Finds domains and subdomains related to a target using public sources. Simple, fast, and easy to pipe into httpx.

title: BBOT
summary: Recursive internet scanner for attack surface management: subdomains, URLs, emails, vuln checks. Scales recon from single domain to whole orgs.

title: SpiderFoot
summary: OSINT automation with 200+ modules querying public data sources about IPs, domains and emails. Good for structured footprinting reports.

title: recon-ng
summary: Modular recon framework with a Metasploit-like console; modules for harvesting and enumeration against a database-backed workspace. Classic taught in many pentest courses.

title: naabu
summary: ProjectDiscovery's fast port scanner written in Go; simpler output and easier automation than masscan for targeted sweeps. Pairs with httpx and nuclei in PD pipelines.

title: masscan
summary: Internet-scale port scanner that can scan the entire IPv4 space in minutes. The tool behind large-scale internet surveys; handle responsibly and know your local rules.

title: RustScan
summary: Extremely fast port scanner that auto-pipes results into nmap for service detection. Community favorite for quick CTF and lab scanning.

title: dnsenum
summary: DNS enumeration script for A, MX, NS records, zone transfers and reverse lookups. Old but dependable DNS recon check.

title: DNSRecon
summary: Python DNS enumeration with brute-forcing, zone transfers, cache snooping and wildcard checks. More feature-complete than dnsenum for DNS recon.

title: THC Hydra
summary: The classic parallelized online password brute-forcer supporting 50+ protocols (SSH, FTP, HTTP forms, SMB). Teaches the reality of weak credentials; use only on authorized targets.

title: John the Ripper
summary: Legendary offline password cracker with huge hash-format support and smart mangling rules. First tool to try on captured hashes.

title: hashcat
summary: World's fastest GPU password cracker, supporting 300+ hash types. The standard for serious offline hash cracking once John is not enough.

title: SharpHound
summary: C# data collector for BloodHound that maps AD users, groups, sessions and trust relationships. Run it, import into BloodHound, find the attack paths.

title: BloodHound.py
summary: Python ingestor for BloodHound that collects AD data without a Windows box. Useful from a Linux attack host when SharpHound is not an option.

title: Coercer
summary: Forces Windows machines to authenticate to an attacker host via MS-RPRN, MS-EFSR and other coercion methods. Triggers the authentication relay and capture attacks.

title: PEASS-ng
summary: Privilege escalation enumeration scripts (LinPEAS, WinPEAS) that highlight misconfigurations and suggest exploits. Run early on any compromised host.

title: RevShells
summary: Online reverse shell generator for dozens of languages with listener commands included. Faster and less error-prone than memorizing payloads.

title: Plaso (log2timeline)
summary: Builds super-timelines from disk images and logs for forensic analysis. Standard engine behind many DFIR timeline workflows.

title: holehe
summary: Checks whether an email address is registered on 120+ sites without alerting the target. Quiet account-discovery for investigations.

title: ExifTool
summary: Reads and writes metadata in images, PDFs and office files. Reveals GPS coordinates, camera models and author names people forget to strip.

title: Maltego
summary: Graph-based link analysis for connecting people, domains, IPs and social accounts visually. The investigation whiteboard of OSINT; Community Edition covers learning.
priceNote: Community Edition free; commercial editions paid.

title: InfoSec Write-ups
summary: Community publication of bug bounty and pentest write-ups. Learn real methodology from other hunters' reports.

title: OffSec
summary: Creators of Kali Linux and the OSCP; 14 hands-on certifications from PEN-200 to advanced exploit dev. The most respected name in offensive security training.
priceNote: Learn One ~$2,749/yr observed 2026-10-01; individual course exams e.g. WEB-200/SOC-200 $1,749; check current price.

title: TCM Security
summary: Practical, affordable training academy with 250+ hours and hands-on certs like PNPT and PJPT. Best value entry into practical pentesting certs.
priceNote: e.g. PSAA $249 observed 2026-10-01; Academy subscriptions and other certs vary; check current price.

summary: GhostPack's C# tool for abusing Active Directory Certificate Services: find misconfigured certificate templates and request certificates that lead to domain admin. Pairs naturally with the ESC attack techniques.
title: Certify

summary: Searches Windows file shares across the network for interesting files: passwords in spreadsheets, private keys, config files. Point it at a domain, go make coffee, come back to results.
title: Snaffler

summary: GhostPack's C# host enumeration tool. Runs a battery of local security checks on a Windows box and reports what is misconfigured. Useful in the first minutes after landing initial access.
title: Seatbelt

summary: GhostPack's C# Windows privilege escalation checker. Audits the local machine for known privesc paths across services, registry, and scheduled tasks, and reports what is actually exploitable.
title: SharpUp

summary: Open-source credential recovery: pulls stored passwords from browsers, Wi-Fi profiles, and dozens of applications on a compromised host. A standard post-exploitation step on Windows and Linux.
title: LaZagne

summary: PowerShell script by itm4n that audits Windows systems for privilege escalation misconfigurations: services, registry keys, scheduled tasks, and access tokens. Run it on every Windows target.
title: PrivescCheck

summary: Microsoft's official Windows troubleshooting toolkit: Process Explorer, Autoruns, TCPView, and dozens more. Indispensable for malware triage and seeing what a Windows box is really doing.
title: Sysinternals Suite

summary: The Swiss army knife for network attacks: MITM, sniffing, spoofing, and Wi-Fi attacks in one Go binary. Replaces a shelf of single-purpose tools.
title: Bettercap

summary: The classic Wi-Fi security auditing suite: capture handshakes and crack WEP and WPA keys. Still the baseline every wireless assessment starts from.
title: Aircrack-ng

summary: Automated wireless auditing: attacks WEP, WPA, and WPS networks with almost no manual steps. A good first wireless tool before learning the manual aircrack-ng workflow.
title: Wifite2

summary: A WinRM shell built for pentesters: pass-the-hash support, file upload and download, loading PowerShell scripts and .NET assemblies in memory. The daily driver on Windows targets.
title: Evil-WinRM

summary: The open-source reverse engineering framework: disassembly, debugging, and binary patching from the command line. Steep learning curve, unmatched once it clicks.
title: Radare2

summary: Decompiles Android APKs back to smali and resources so you can read and modify app code. The first step in almost every Android assessment.
title: Apktool

summary: Condensed command reference for incident responders: Windows and Linux commands for triage, memory capture, and log analysis. Built to sit next to your keyboard during an incident.
title: Blue Team Field Manual

summary: Michal Zalewski's deep dive into how browsers really work and where their security boundaries break. The book that explains why web attacks are possible at all.
title: The Tangled Web

summary: Zalewski's classic on passive network reconnaissance: what your traffic gives away even when you think it does not. The concepts still hold.
title: Silence on the Wire

summary: SANS maintains a public index of their one-page cheat sheets: Windows forensics, memory analysis, network forensics, log analysis. Print the ones for your current topic.
title: SANS Cheat Sheets Index

summary: The OWASP Mobile Application Security Testing Guide: the standard methodology for testing iOS and Android apps, with concrete test cases for every control.
title: OWASP MAS Testing Guide

summary: WonderHowTo's hacking tutorial channel: short practical videos on Wi-Fi hacking, phishing labs, and beginner-friendly walkthroughs.
title: Null Byte

summary: Weekly cybersecurity news in plain language: breaches, vulnerabilities, and privacy stories explained without hype.
title: Seytonic
